overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's account of the primacy of perception. You'll be asked about his critique of empiricism and intellectualism, the perceptual field and constancy, and the incomplete reduction.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: An empiricist explains the Müller-Lyer illusion by saying the lines produce equal sensations and perception adds an error. What assumption does Merleau-Ponty find here?

options.html: That illusions are caused by fatigue or inattention
options.text: That illusions are caused by fatigue or inattention
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sensation and association.

options.html: That what we sense is fixed by the stimulus in advance
options.text: That what we sense is fixed by the stimulus in advance
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the constancy hypothesis, which decides in advance what perception must contain.

options.html: That the two lines are in fact unequal in length
options.text: That the two lines are in fact unequal in length
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sensation and association.

options.html: That perception can never be mistaken about anything
options.text: That perception can never be mistaken about anything
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sensation and association.

forms.stemHtml: After measuring the Müller-Lyer lines and learning they're equal, you still see them as unequal. Which theory does this most directly challenge?

options.html: Empiricism, since the sensations must have changed
options.text: Empiricism, since the sensations must have changed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention, judgment, and the prejudice of the world.

options.html: Intellectualism, since a new judgment doesn't correct it
options.text: Intellectualism, since a new judgment doesn't correct it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If perceiving were judging, knowing the truth would change the perception. It doesn't.

options.html: Gestalt psychology, since the figure should reverse
options.text: Gestalt psychology, since the figure should reverse
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention, judgment, and the prejudice of the world.

options.html: Neither, since both predict the illusion will persist
options.text: Neither, since both predict the illusion will persist
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention, judgment, and the prejudice of the world.

forms.stemHtml: What is the name for the assumption that each local stimulus produces a fixed, corresponding sensation, whatever its context? Enter two words.

options.html: constancy hypothesis
options.text: constancy hypothesis
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty, following the Gestalt psychologists, argues that perception constantly violates it.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sensation and association.

forms.stemHtml: At the edge of your visual field, you can tell something is moving but not its color or shape. How does Merleau-Ponty treat this?

options.html: As a defect of vision that science should correct
options.text: As a defect of vision that science should correct
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on figure, ground, and the perceptual field.

options.html: As genuine indeterminacy belonging to the field
options.text: As genuine indeterminacy belonging to the field
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The margins belong to the field positively. What appears there is indeterminate, not a determinate thing seen badly.

options.html: As a figure temporarily hidden by the ground
options.text: As a figure temporarily hidden by the ground
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on figure, ground, and the perceptual field.

options.html: As a memory projected onto the field's edges
options.text: As a memory projected onto the field's edges
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on figure, ground, and the perceptual field.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following describe the optimum, on Merleau-Ponty's account? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A distance at which an object is given most fully
options.text: A distance at which an object is given most fully
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The optimum is the best view of an object for a given purpose.

options.html: A norm against which other views count as deviations
options.text: A norm against which other views count as deviations
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Other appearances are lived as deviations from the optimum.

options.html: The point at which the brain stops correcting input
options.text: The point at which the brain stops correcting input
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on constancy and the optimum.

options.html: The brightest lighting under which colors appear
options.text: The brightest lighting under which colors appear
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on constancy and the optimum.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term for the hidden sides and further details of a perceived object itself, such as the back of a house seen from the street? Enter two words.

options.html: inner horizon
options.text: inner horizon
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The inner horizon is co-present, not imagined or inferred.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on horizons and motivation.

forms.stemHtml: How does Merleau-Ponty distinguish phenomenology from reflective analysis?

options.html: Reflective analysis describes; phenomenology explains
options.text: Reflective analysis describes; phenomenology explains
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

options.html: Reflective analysis rebuilds experience from a mind's acts
options.text: Reflective analysis rebuilds experience from a mind's acts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Reflective analysis reconstructs experience as if the mind had built the world. Phenomenology describes how it's given.

options.html: Reflective analysis uses experiments; phenomenology doesn't
options.text: Reflective analysis uses experiments; phenomenology doesn't
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

options.html: Reflective analysis studies the body; phenomenology the mind
options.text: Reflective analysis studies the body; phenomenology the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

forms.stemHtml: Critics of the 1946 address objected that grounding knowledge in perception leads to relativism. How did Merleau-Ponty reply?

options.html: By conceding that all truth is relative to perceivers
options.text: By conceding that all truth is relative to perceivers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

options.html: By holding that the perceived world is shared
options.text: By holding that the perceived world is shared
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Perception opens onto a common world, seen from other sides by others, so it isn't private.

options.html: By grounding truth in mathematics instead of perception
options.text: By grounding truth in mathematics instead of perception
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

options.html: By denying that perception is ever perspectival
options.text: By denying that perception is ever perspectival
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

forms.stemHtml: How does Merleau-Ponty's use of the reduction differ from Husserl's, as the comparison presents it?

options.html: Merleau-Ponty rejects the epoché, and Husserl keeps it
options.text: Merleau-Ponty rejects the epoché, and Husserl keeps it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing Husserl and Merleau-Ponty on the reduction.

options.html: Merleau-Ponty holds that it reveals our ties to the world
options.text: Merleau-Ponty holds that it reveals our ties to the world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! For Merleau-Ponty, the reduction reveals being-in-the-world, not a pure constituting consciousness.

options.html: Merleau-Ponty treats it as a form of doubt
options.text: Merleau-Ponty treats it as a form of doubt
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing Husserl and Merleau-Ponty on the reduction.

options.html: Merleau-Ponty holds that it can be completed at once
options.text: Merleau-Ponty holds that it can be completed at once
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing Husserl and Merleau-Ponty on the reduction.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following describe the primacy of perception? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The perceived world is presupposed by all knowledge
options.text: The perceived world is presupposed by all knowledge
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Science, logic, and ethics build on and depend on it.

options.html: It concerns foundation, not the claim that all is perception
options.text: It concerns foundation, not the claim that all is perception
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! "Primacy" doesn't reduce ideas or values to perceptions.

options.html: Perception already has meaning before explicit thought
options.text: Perception already has meaning before explicit thought
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is perception as a nascent logos.

options.html: Scientific knowledge is inferior to perception
options.text: Scientific knowledge is inferior to perception
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

options.html: Truth depends only on the individual perceiver
options.text: Truth depends only on the individual perceiver
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty argue that memory can't supply the meaning of what we perceive?

options.html: Because memories are always less vivid than perceptions
options.text: Because memories are always less vivid than perceptions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sensation and association.

options.html: Because recall already requires an organized present
options.text: Because recall already requires an organized present
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! To call up the right memory, the present perception must already be organized enough to resemble it.

options.html: Because we don't remember most of what we perceive
options.text: Because we don't remember most of what we perceive
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sensation and association.

options.html: Because memories are stored in a different part of the brain
options.text: Because memories are stored in a different part of the brain
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sensation and association.

forms.stemHtml: In The Structure of Behavior, what distinguishes the vital order from the physical order?

options.html: Living organisms are made of more complex matter
options.text: Living organisms are made of more complex matter
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Merleau-Ponty's sources.

options.html: Organisms maintain themselves in their own milieu
options.text: Organisms maintain themselves in their own milieu
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Living organisms actively maintain themselves, responding to what matters for their life.

options.html: Organisms respond to symbolic and cultural meanings
options.text: Organisms respond to symbolic and cultural meanings
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Merleau-Ponty's sources.

options.html: Organisms follow fixed reflexes to local stimuli
options.text: Organisms follow fixed reflexes to local stimuli
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Merleau-Ponty's sources.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's name for the assumption that the determinate, objective world of science is given first and can be read back into perception as its starting point? Enter the four-word phrase.

options.html: prejudice of the world
options.text: prejudice of the world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Empiricism and intellectualism share this prejudice.

options.html: the prejudice of the world
options.text: the prejudice of the world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Empiricism and intellectualism share this prejudice.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention, judgment, and the prejudice of the world.

forms.stemHtml: A white wall in dim evening light is still seen as white. How does Merleau-Ponty describe this?

options.html: The brain calculates the wall's true color from the light
options.text: The brain calculates the wall's true color from the light
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on constancy and the optimum.

options.html: The mind judges that walls are usually white
options.text: The mind judges that walls are usually white
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on constancy and the optimum.

options.html: The wall is seen as white relative to a lighting level
options.text: The wall is seen as white relative to a lighting level
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Lighting is a level we see with, and colors appear relative to it.

options.html: Memory of the wall in daylight fills in its color
options.text: Memory of the wall in daylight fills in its color
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sensation and association.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are examples of a perceived object's horizons? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The far side of a mug on your desk
options.text: The far side of a mug on your desk
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is part of the mug's inner horizon.

options.html: The room surrounding the mug
options.text: The room surrounding the mug
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is part of the mug's outer horizon.

options.html: The inside of the mug you can't see
options.text: The inside of the mug you can't see
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is also part of the mug's inner horizon.

options.html: A picture of the mug you imagine
options.text: A picture of the mug you imagine
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on horizons and motivation.

options.html: The mug's color as you see it now
options.text: The mug's color as you see it now
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on horizons and motivation.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term, borrowed from Husserl, for a relation of sense in which one perceived feature makes another appropriate without causing it or implying it logically? Enter one word.

options.html: motivation
options.text: motivation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty sets motivation against both causation and inference.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on horizons and motivation.

forms.stemHtml: Merleau-Ponty compares scientific knowledge of the world to geography. What point does the comparison make?

options.html: That science is less accurate than everyday perception
options.text: That science is less accurate than everyday perception
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

options.html: That science presupposes the world first given in experience
options.text: That science presupposes the world first given in experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! As a map presupposes the countryside, scientific knowledge presupposes the world as first experienced.

options.html: That science and perception study different worlds
options.text: That science and perception study different worlds
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

options.html: That maps are the best model for describing experience
options.text: That maps are the best model for describing experience
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

forms.stemHtml: What does Merleau-Ponty mean by calling perception a "nascent logos"?

options.html: That perception is a primitive form of language
options.text: That perception is a primitive form of language
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

options.html: That perception must be corrected by logic
options.text: That perception must be corrected by logic
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

options.html: That reason and meaning already arise in perception
options.text: That reason and meaning already arise in perception
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Perception isn't irrational raw material. Meaning and order are already at work in it.

options.html: That perception is a form of unconscious reasoning
options.text: That perception is a form of unconscious reasoning
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following is an example of act intentionality?

options.html: A landscape showing up as peaceful at a glance
options.text: A landscape showing up as peaceful at a glance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on essences and operative intentionality.

options.html: A staircase inviting you to climb it
options.text: A staircase inviting you to climb it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on essences and operative intentionality.

options.html: Deciding to buy a house after weighing options
options.text: Deciding to buy a house after weighing options
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Deciding is an explicit act that posits an object. That's act intentionality.

options.html: A face looking friendly before any thought
options.text: A face looking friendly before any thought
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on essences and operative intentionality.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are claims Merleau-Ponty makes about the incomplete reduction? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Its incompleteness is its most important lesson
options.text: Its incompleteness is its most important lesson
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The famous claim turns an apparent failure into a finding.

options.html: What resists suspension reveals being-in-the-world
options.text: What resists suspension reveals being-in-the-world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The residue shows we're rooted in the world before reflection.

options.html: The reduction should therefore be abandoned
options.text: The reduction should therefore be abandoned
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

options.html: It proves that phenomenology is merely subjective
options.text: It proves that phenomenology is merely subjective
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty say both classical theories make attention powerless?

options.html: Because both deny that attention exists at all
options.text: Because both deny that attention exists at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention, judgment, and the prejudice of the world.

options.html: Because in both it only uncovers a finished content
options.text: Because in both it only uncovers a finished content
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Whether the content is in sensation or in thought, attention adds nothing. Merleau-Ponty holds that attention transforms the field.

options.html: Because both claim attention is controlled by the body
options.text: Because both claim attention is controlled by the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention, judgment, and the prejudice of the world.

options.html: Because both treat attention as a kind of emotion
options.text: Because both treat attention as a kind of emotion
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention, judgment, and the prejudice of the world.

forms.stemHtml: How does Merleau-Ponty's position relate to empiricism and intellectualism?

options.html: He combines their best features into a middle view
options.text: He combines their best features into a middle view
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing empiricism, intellectualism, and Merleau-Ponty.

options.html: He sides with intellectualism against empiricism
options.text: He sides with intellectualism against empiricism
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing empiricism, intellectualism, and Merleau-Ponty.

options.html: He rejects the premise both theories share
options.text: He rejects the premise both theories share
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both read the determinate world of science back into perception. Merleau-Ponty changes the starting point.

options.html: He sides with empiricism against intellectualism
options.text: He sides with empiricism against intellectualism
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing empiricism, intellectualism, and Merleau-Ponty.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term for the field of experience as it's actually lived, before it's recast in terms of objective sensations or acts of thought? Enter two words.

options.html: phenomenal field
options.text: phenomenal field
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty recommends a return to the phenomenal field.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention, judgment, and the prejudice of the world.

forms.stemHtml: How does Merleau-Ponty describe depth?

options.html: As a third dimension seen from the side, like width
options.text: As a third dimension seen from the side, like width
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the thing as style and depth.

options.html: As a conclusion inferred from cues like convergence
options.text: As a conclusion inferred from cues like convergence
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the thing as style and depth.

options.html: As a lived relation between the perceiver and things
options.text: As a lived relation between the perceiver and things
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Depth expresses the perceiver's involvement in the world, which is why he calls it the most "existential" dimension.

options.html: As an illusion produced by the two eyes' images
options.text: As an illusion produced by the two eyes' images
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the thing as style and depth.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following fit Merleau-Ponty's account of the thing as a unity of style? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A glass's fragility is visible in its transparency
options.text: A glass's fragility is visible in its transparency
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each property expresses the others.

options.html: We recognize a thing's manner of being as a whole
options.text: We recognize a thing's manner of being as a whole
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! We recognize a thing by its style, as we recognize a person by their gait.

options.html: A thing is a bundle of separate properties
options.text: A thing is a bundle of separate properties
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the thing as style and depth.

options.html: Properties are added to a substance one by one
options.text: Properties are added to a substance one by one
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the thing as style and depth.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term for the unified manner of being that a perceived thing expresses through all its properties? Enter one word.

options.html: style
options.text: style
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each property of a thing expresses its style.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the thing as style and depth.

forms.stemHtml: What role does Merleau-Ponty give to essences?

options.html: The final goal that replaces the world with ideas
options.text: The final goal that replaces the world with ideas
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on essences and operative intentionality.

options.html: A means of describing the meaning experience has
options.text: A means of describing the meaning experience has
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Essences help bring experience's meaning to light. They aren't the goal.

options.html: A mistake that phenomenology should abandon
options.text: A mistake that phenomenology should abandon
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on essences and operative intentionality.

options.html: Mental images from which perception is built
options.text: Mental images from which perception is built
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on essences and operative intentionality.

forms.stemHtml: How does Merleau-Ponty characterize the truth that perception gives?

options.html: Absolute and guaranteed in advance
options.text: Absolute and guaranteed in advance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

options.html: Private to each perceiver
options.text: Private to each perceiver
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

options.html: Presumptive, open, and revisable
options.text: Presumptive, open, and revisable
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Perceptual truth is presumed, confirmed, and corrected as experience continues, which makes it revisable, not arbitrary.

options.html: Arbitrary and without standards
options.text: Arbitrary and without standards
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the primacy of perception and its critics.

forms.stemHtml: What does the image of loosening, rather than cutting, the intentional threads convey?

options.html: That the reduction takes us outside the world
options.text: That the reduction takes us outside the world
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

options.html: That our ties to the world become visible but remain
options.text: That our ties to the world become visible but remain
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Loosening makes the ties appear. They can't be cut, because the reflecting subject stays in the world.

options.html: That the world gradually disappears from view
options.text: That the world gradually disappears from view
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

options.html: That consciousness produces the world's meaning
options.text: That consciousness produces the world's meaning
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on description and the reduction.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are true of operative intentionality? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It is pre-reflective
options.text: It is pre-reflective
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It works before any explicit act.

options.html: It is largely bodily
options.text: It is largely bodily
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty locates it chiefly in the body's grip on the world.

options.html: It establishes the unity of the world
options.text: It establishes the unity of the world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It establishes the unity of the world and of our life.

options.html: It consists of explicit judgments
options.text: It consists of explicit judgments
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on essences and operative intentionality.

options.html: It is the same as unconscious inference
options.text: It is the same as unconscious inference
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on essences and operative intentionality.
